roles.title: Toastmaster of the Day
roles.purpose: You are the conductor of the meeting. You keep the flow smooth and the energy warm.

before: Check with Timer and Table Topics Master
during: Start on time and set a friendly tone
Introduce each segment clearly
Keep the meeting flowing (move forward gently)
after: Thank guests, role takers, and speakers

tips: Smile first. People relax when you do 😊
Short transitions are better than perfect transitions.
If you forget something, pause and continue. Everyone is on your side.
scripts: Good evening everyone, welcome to our meeting!
Tonight, our theme is __________.
Now we will move to our next segment: __________.
Thank you everyone for your wonderful participation. See you next time!

roles.title: Timer
roles.purpose: You protect fairness and rhythm. Timing helps everyone improve and keeps the meeting on track.

during: Start timing when the speaker begins
Show signals at the correct milestones
Record times clearly

tips: Be consistent. The club trusts your accuracy.
If you miss a signal, stay calm and continue.
scripts: For this segment, the time is __________ minutes.
Timing results: Speaker 1: ____, Speaker 2: ____.

roles.title: Table Topics Master
roles.purpose: You create fun, safe, short speaking opportunities. You help members practice thinking on their feet.

before: Check if there are guests (make it extra easy)
during: Explain the rules and time limit
Call one person at a time
Encourage applause and keep it light

tips: Choose topics that are easy to start.
If someone is nervous, offer a simpler question.
scripts: Now we begin Table Topics. This is a 1–2 minute impromptu speaking segment.
Our next speaker is __________. Please come up!
Your topic is: __________.
Thank you! Let’s give __________ a big hand.

roles.title: Evaluator
roles.purpose: You help the speaker grow with supportive feedback. Your job is to encourage first, then guide.

before: Read the speaker objectives / project goals
Ask the speaker what feedback they want
during: Observe structure, clarity, and delivery
Write strengths and 1–2 improvement ideas
Note one memorable moment

tips: Be kind and specific. Specific helps more than strong opinions.
One improvement is enough. Don’t overload.
Smile. Your tone matters more than your words.
scripts: Thank you, __________. I really enjoyed your speech, especially __________.
One strength I noticed is __________.
One suggestion to make it even stronger is __________.
Overall, great job — keep going!

roles.title: Language Evaluator
roles.purpose: You help the club speak better by noticing good words, grammar, and clear expressions.

before: Decide what to observe (grammar, vocabulary, clarity)
during: Note strong phrases and good vocabulary
Note common language issues gently

scripts: Today’s Word of the Day is: __________ (meaning: __________).
Great phrases I heard today include: __________.
One small reminder for us: __________.

roles.title: Ah-Counter
roles.purpose: You help speakers become more confident by reducing filler words and distracting habits.

before: Decide what to track (ah/um, repeats, filler, habits)
during: Track each speaker fairly and quietly
Note one helpful observation per speaker
after: Keep the tone light and encouraging

tips: Be factual, not funny at someone’s expense.
We all have fillers — this role helps everyone.
scripts: Ah-counter report: I noted filler words such as ah/um, repeated words, and pauses.
Today’s results: __________.

roles.title: Speaker
roles.purpose: You share an idea and practice communication. Your goal is progress, not perfection.

during: Speak a bit slower than normal
Pause between points
Look up and connect
after: Listen to feedback with an open mind

tips: Nervous is normal. It means you care.
A pause feels long to you, but it feels confident to the audience.
scripts: Good evening everyone. Today I’d like to share __________.
The first point is __________.
To conclude, __________. Thank you.

roles.title: General Evaluator
roles.purpose: You help the whole meeting improve — structure, timing, energy, and quality of evaluations.

before: Confirm meeting agenda and evaluation flow
during: Observe meeting flow and timing
Observe how evaluations support growth
Note 2 strengths and 1 improvement for the meeting
after: Thank role takers and encourage improvement

tips: Focus on the meeting system, not individuals.
Keep it balanced: praise + one suggestion.
scripts: Overall, the meeting was strong because __________.
One suggestion to improve our next meeting is __________.
Thank you everyone for serving and participating.
